questions.questionText: Aman starts walking towards North and covers 3 km. Then Aman turns right and walks 2 km, and finally turns right and walks 2 km. In which direction is Aman walking now?
questions.hint: Trace each turn sequentially from the standard compass rose (NESW).
questions.explanation: A right turn from North is East, and another right turn leads to South. Therefore, Aman is finally walking towards South.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Start facing North.
Step 2: First turn (turns right) sets the intermediate direction.
Step 3: Final turn (turns right) leads to facing South.
questions.memoryTip: Clockwise sequence of cardinal directions is always N -> E -> S -> W.

questions.questionText: Priya starts from point P and travels 3 km towards North, then turns right and travels 4 km to reach point Q. What is the shortest distance between points P and Q?
questions.hint: Apply Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse = √(Base² + Perpendicular²).
questions.explanation: The path forms a right-angled triangle with perpendicular legs 3 km and 4 km. By Pythagoras theorem: Shortest Distance = √(3² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = √(25) = 5 km.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Identify the displacement components: 3 km along North and 4 km after turning right.
Step 2: Note the right-angle formed between the two paths.
Step 3: Compute √(3² + 4²) = 5 km.
questions.memoryTip: Remember common Pythagorean triplets: (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (6, 8, 10), (8, 15, 17), (7, 24, 25).

questions.hint: Resolve the net horizontal (East-West) and net vertical (North-South) displacements separately.
questions.explanation: Net North-South displacement = 10 m North - 4 m South = 6 m North. Net East-West displacement = 12 m East - 4 m West = 8 m East. Shortest distance = √(6² + 8²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 m. Since net coordinates are (+East, +North), the direction from X to Y is North-East.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Calculate vertical displacement: North - South = 10 - 4 = 6 m North.
Step 2: Calculate horizontal displacement: East - West = 12 - 4 = 8 m East.
Step 3: Distance = √(6² + 8²) = 10 m.
Step 4: Relative direction is North-East.
questions.memoryTip: Net displacement method: Group all North/South movements together and all East/West movements together.

questions.explanation: Net North-South displacement = 30 m North - 22 m South = 8 m North. Net East-West displacement = 12 m East - 6 m West = 6 m East. Shortest distance = √(8² + 6²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 m. Since net coordinates are (+East, +North), the direction from X to Y is North-East.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Calculate vertical displacement: North - South = 30 - 22 = 8 m North.
Step 2: Calculate horizontal displacement: East - West = 12 - 6 = 6 m East.
Step 3: Distance = √(8² + 6²) = 10 m.
Step 4: Relative direction is North-East.
questions.memoryTip: Net displacement method: Group all North/South movements together and all East/West movements together.

questions.explanation: Net North-South displacement = 15 m North - 7 m South = 8 m North. Net East-West displacement = 24 m East - 18 m West = 6 m East. Shortest distance = √(8² + 6²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 m. Since net coordinates are (+East, +North), the direction from X to Y is North-East.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Calculate vertical displacement: North - South = 15 - 7 = 8 m North.
Step 2: Calculate horizontal displacement: East - West = 24 - 18 = 6 m East.
Step 3: Distance = √(8² + 6²) = 10 m.
Step 4: Relative direction is North-East.
questions.memoryTip: Net displacement method: Group all North/South movements together and all East/West movements together.

questions.explanation: Net North-South displacement = 25 m North - 17 m South = 8 m North. Net East-West displacement = 20 m East - 14 m West = 6 m East. Shortest distance = √(8² + 6²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 m. Since net coordinates are (+East, +North), the direction from X to Y is North-East.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Calculate vertical displacement: North - South = 25 - 17 = 8 m North.
Step 2: Calculate horizontal displacement: East - West = 20 - 14 = 6 m East.
Step 3: Distance = √(8² + 6²) = 10 m.
Step 4: Relative direction is North-East.
questions.memoryTip: Net displacement method: Group all North/South movements together and all East/West movements together.

questions.explanation: Net North-South displacement = 10 m North - 2 m South = 8 m North. Net East-West displacement = 16 m East - 10 m West = 6 m East. Shortest distance = √(8² + 6²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 m. Since net coordinates are (+East, +North), the direction from X to Y is North-East.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Calculate vertical displacement: North - South = 10 - 2 = 8 m North.
Step 2: Calculate horizontal displacement: East - West = 16 - 10 = 6 m East.
Step 3: Distance = √(8² + 6²) = 10 m.
Step 4: Relative direction is North-East.
questions.memoryTip: Net displacement method: Group all North/South movements together and all East/West movements together.

questions.explanation: Net North-South displacement = 20 m North - 12 m South = 8 m North. Net East-West displacement = 12 m East - 6 m West = 6 m East. Shortest distance = √(8² + 6²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 m. Since net coordinates are (+East, +North), the direction from X to Y is North-East.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Calculate vertical displacement: North - South = 20 - 12 = 8 m North.
Step 2: Calculate horizontal displacement: East - West = 12 - 6 = 6 m East.
Step 3: Distance = √(8² + 6²) = 10 m.
Step 4: Relative direction is North-East.
questions.memoryTip: Net displacement method: Group all North/South movements together and all East/West movements together.

questions.questionText: One morning after sunrise, Aman and Rohit were standing in a garden facing each other. If the shadow of Rohit fell exactly to the left of Aman, which direction was Aman facing?
questions.hint: In the morning, the Sun is in the East, so all shadows point towards the West.
questions.explanation: In the morning, the sun is in the East; hence, every object casts its shadow towards the West. For the shadow to fall to the left of Aman, Aman's left must be pointing West. When a person faces North, their left points to the West. Therefore, Aman was facing North.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Time is morning (sunrise) -> Sun is in East -> All shadows fall towards West.
Step 2: The shadow falls to the left of Aman -> Aman's left is West.
Step 3: A person whose left is West must be facing North.
questions.memoryTip: Sunrise Rule: Facing North -> Shadow is on Left. Facing South -> Shadow is on Right.

questions.questionText: One morning, Divya was performing yoga with head down and feet up facing North. In which direction will Divya's right hand point?
questions.hint: In headstand / inverted posture, left and right hands swap directions compared to standing upright.
questions.explanation: When standing upright facing North, the right hand points East. In an inverted headstand facing North, the body orientation reverses lateral symmetry, so the right hand points West.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Normal upright posture facing North: Left = West, Right = East.

Step 3: Right hand points to West.
questions.memoryTip: Headstand rule: Hand directions reverse compared to normal upright orientation.

questions.questionText: At 12:00 noon on a sunny day in June, in which direction does a vertical flagpole cast its shadow?
options: No shadow / negligible right under base
questions.hint: At solar noon, the Sun is directly overhead at zenith.
questions.explanation: At exactly 12:00 noon, the Sun is directly overhead (zenith) in the sky. Therefore, vertical objects cast virtually no lateral shadow or the shadow falls directly underneath the base.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Solar position at 12 noon is directly overhead.
Step 2: Rays strike vertically downwards.
Step 3: No lateral shadow is cast in any cardinal direction.
questions.memoryTip: At 12 noon, shadows have zero length horizontally because the sun is directly overhead.
